page.title: Bandwidth & path diagnostics
page.description: Run on demand, separately from traffic metrics, baselines, and severity.

historyTable.empty: No completed diagnostic tests match these filters and period.
historyTable.testHelp: This result is not valid for LAN bottleneck analysis.
historyTable.contextHelp: Local link speed is not available bandwidth. The local route shows the interface/next hop; MTR shows responding Layer-3 hops.
historyTable.pathHelp: MTR shows only responding Layer-3 hops, not every physical switch, cable, bridged access point, or patch panel. A label means that IP is known in manual inventory, not proof of every traversed Layer-2 device.
historyTable.noPath: No path measurement is associated with this job.

chart.empty: No completed diagnostic tests match these filters and period.
chart.ariaLabel: Upload and download Mbps over time

workspace.loadError: Runner status or diagnostic data could not be loaded.
workspace.chooseTarget: Select an authorized target so the local runner can determine the correct interface and route.
workspace.sourceHelp: Enter a physical location name, not an IP. The runner detects the source IPv4 automatically.
workspace.activeTraffic: iperf3 generates active traffic. The test runs only after a click and is limited to {{count}} seconds per direction.
workspace.viewerNotice: Viewers can read results, but the Operator role is required to start an active bandwidth diagnostic.
workspace.iperfUnavailable: Bandwidth testing is disabled because the iperf3 server is unavailable on TCP {{port}}.
workspace.noJob: No active or saved diagnostic job yet.
workspace.runnerReady: Online and ready to receive structured jobs.
workspace.runnerOffline: Offline or heartbeat is older than 30 seconds.
workspace.linkHelp: Local link speed is the runner's negotiated link, not available bandwidth or an iperf3 result.
workspace.icmpNotice: No ICMP response does not automatically mean the target is offline; the host or firewall may block ping.
workspace.pathStored: Path details are saved in the session history.
workspace.pathStoredHelp: Open only the session you want to inspect so the latest result is not duplicated on this page.
workspace.noTarget: No authorized LAN diagnostic target is configured.
workspace.noTargetHelp: An admin must add an authorized iperf3 server IP through the local scripts/configure_diagnostic_target.py tool, then restart the runner. See docs/PANDUAN.md. The browser does not accept arbitrary target IPs and never silently falls back to localhost.
workspace.testEnvironmentHelp: Not valid for LAN performance analysis. Values only verify the pipeline.
workspace.requestFailed: Diagnostic request failed. Check the runner, target, and preflight result.

interpretation.title: Interpretation
interpretation.interface: The measurement used the {{connection}} interface selected by the Windows route to the target.
interpretation.link: The local link negotiated at {{speed}}; this is not available bandwidth.
interpretation.wifi: The test includes the wireless path and cannot by itself prove a wired LAN bottleneck.
interpretation.ethernet: The measurement used the Ethernet interface selected by the operating system for the target.
interpretation.loss: Layer-3 packet loss was observed up to {{loss}}%.
interpretation.noLoss: No significant Layer-3 packet loss was found on responding hops.
interpretation.onLink: The target is on-link; the physical Layer-2 path is not visible through MTR.
interpretation.routed: MTR only shows responding Layer-3 hops.
interpretation.compare: Compare other locations against the same server to narrow the suspected bottleneck; this result does not confirm a failed physical device.

panel.title: Per-session result history
panel.description: Use filters to compare results. Path details open per session so they do not mix with the active/latest job panel above.
panel.loadError: Diagnostic data could not be loaded
panel.loadErrorHelp: Check the diagnostics Edge Function deployment, login session, and RLS.
panel.comparisonHelp: Numerical comparison across locations and connection types for the selected target.
panel.historyHelp: Select one source, target, and connection type so one history uses one scale.
panel.selectFilters: Complete all three filters to display the historical chart.
panel.pathHelp: Select one session to see responding Layer-3 hops, latency, and loss in order.
panel.wifi: WiFi measures client-to-server end to end and is not proof of a wired LAN bottleneck.
panel.mtr: MTR shows responding Layer-3 hops and does not reveal every Layer-2 switch.
panel.suspected: Differences in results indicate a suspected bottleneck; they do not prove a specific device has failed.
